minutes.headline: Finance Committee pushed its reorganization, split no minutes yet, and floated a written policy for changed capital scope.
minutes.summary: A short summer meeting with a new member welcomed. Reorganization and clerk selection were deferred until a fuller committee; liaison assignments were adjusted informally. Members discussed a need for a written policy when a capital project's scope changes, heard a town manager report on bids and abatements, and a volunteer offered to write the outstanding minutes.

what_happened.line: The Finance Committee deferred its reorganization and clerk selection to the next meeting, when more members are expected to be present.
A member will contact the chairs of other boards about a written policy for when a capital project's scope changes.
A volunteer offered to write the minutes for all outstanding past meetings, replacing the plan to divide them among members.
The town manager reported that a single Town Hall roof bid was too high, so the roof and chimneys will be rebid first in phases.
The August 10 meeting will likely not be held for lack of a quorum; the next meeting is probably August 24.

why_it_matters: A written rule on changed capital scope would set how the committee reviews a project whose plan shifts after the capital vote, such as the Town Hall roof rebid, which affects how town capital spending is approved.
Minutes for past meetings remain unwritten, so residents have no record of those Finance Committee discussions until the volunteer finishes them.
watch_next: The next Finance Committee meeting, probably August 24, for reorganization, clerk selection and the full liaison list.
Any written policy on changed capital project scope that comes from the outreach to other boards.
